text: I'll start by looking at the workspace.

The rounding is Python's built-in `round()`, which uses banker's rounding (half-to-even) on exact halves, and float representation makes it worse. 10.00 × 0.0725 = 0.725 exactly in decimal, but in binary float it's 0.72499999... or the half case goes to even (0.72). The test name says "half up". Let me confirm the float value.
The full suite has 3 failures, all on exact-half boundaries. That matches the report. I have enough to diagnose.

args.root_cause: calculate_tax() rounds with Python's built-in round(amount * rate, 2). Python's round() uses round-half-to-even (banker's rounding) and operates on binary floats, so when the exact tax lands on a half-cent boundary (e.g. 10.00 * 0.0725 = 0.725), it can round down to the even cent (0.72) instead of the expected half-up value (0.73). Because the tie-breaking goes to the even digit, roughly half of boundary cases round down, which explains the one-directional (under-charge) and boundary-only pattern in the audit. The function's own name/test expectation ("rounds half up to the cent") is not what the code does. Note total_with_tax() also uses round(), but it only rounds an already-2-decimal sum, so the defect originates in calculate_tax(). The discount path (library/pricing.py -> total_with_tax) inherits the same error, as shown by test_pricing.
